headline: Carey’s walk-off 3-run homer lifts St. Lucie Mets past Jupiter 11-10 in 12-inning season finale
teaser: Dylan Carey hit a 422-foot walk-off three-run homer in the bottom of the 12th inning as the St. Lucie Mets closed the 2026 season with a wild 11-10 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads.
body:
Dylan Carey ended the St. Lucie Mets’ 2026 season in dramatic fashion Sunday, launching a 422-foot walk-off three-run homer in the bottom of the 12th inning to give the Mets an 11-10 victory over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Clover Park.

The win capped a chaotic season finale that began Saturday before being suspended and completed Sunday. St. Lucie won five of its final six games and finished the year 58-72 overall and 25-39 in the second half. The Mets finished ahead of Jupiter in the second-half standings and ahead of Daytona overall for third place in the Florida State League East.

## A quiet game turns wild in the ninth

The Mets carried a 6-2 lead into the ninth inning before the game changed quickly.

Reliever Christian Rodriguez walked the first three Jupiter batters, then recorded two groundouts that brought home two runs and cut St. Lucie’s lead to 6-4. PJ Morlando followed with a double, keeping the inning alive for Jacob Lombard.

With Jupiter down to its final strike, Lombard hit a three-run homer to put the Hammerheads ahead 7-6.

St. Lucie answered with two outs in the bottom of the ninth. Ryan Tayman and Yovanny Rodriguez drew back-to-back walks before Kuhio Aloy delivered a two-strike RBI single to right field, tying the game 7-7 and forcing extra innings.

## Both teams trade runs in extras

Each team brought home its automatic runner in the 10th inning.

Josh Hogue hit a two-out, two-strike RBI double off Miguel Mejias to give Jupiter an 8-7 lead. In the bottom half, Reed Stallman scored from third on a one-out wild pitch by Yenfri Sosa to tie the game again at 8-8.

Neither team scored in the 11th.

Jupiter broke through in the top of the 12th when Jeremy Almonte hit a two-run homer off Brett Banks, putting the Hammerheads ahead 10-8.

Sosa returned for the bottom of the inning and opened with a strikeout before issuing a walk. That brought Carey, the Mets’ No. 9 hitter, to the plate as the potential winning run.

Carey drove a 1-0 slider 422 feet to left field for the walk-off three-run homer, giving St. Lucie an 11-10 win. It was the second professional home run for Carey, an undrafted product out of Nebraska.

## Mets use franchise-record 11 pitchers

St. Lucie used a franchise-record 11 pitchers across the suspended game.

Alex Petrovic, a sixth-round pick out of Auburn, started Saturday and made his professional debut. When play resumed Sunday, Luke McNeillie, a fifth-round pick out of Florida; Landon Koenig, an eighth-round pick out of Ole Miss; and Gavin Guidry, a 16th-round pick out of LSU, each made their professional debuts and threw a scoreless inning.

Banks worked the final two innings and earned the win despite allowing Almonte’s go-ahead homer in the 12th.

Jupiter outhit St. Lucie 11-7 and outhit the Mets in all five games of the series, but St. Lucie won four of the five games.

Aloy was the only Met with multiple hits, going 2-for-5 with two singles, a walk and three runs scored.

The game lasted 3 hours, 58 minutes, making it St. Lucie’s longest game of the season. It also included three delays totaling 1 hour, 33 minutes: one before the game began Saturday, another after the first out in the bottom of the first inning Saturday and a third for an umpire change in the 11th inning Sunday.

The Mets finished 6-1 in extra-inning games in 2026. Sunday’s victory was their sixth walk-off win of the season at Clover Park.
